lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Leafs finally looked like a team tired of explaining itself. Friday's 3-1 win over Boston, powered by Morgan Rielly's two goals and his 100th NHL marker, restored some swagger - and gave Toronto consecutive victories after a four-game stumble. Anthony Stolarz stopped 27 shots, but the celebration came with a bill: Chris Tanev left early with a lower-body injury and did not return. That matters for a club sitting 12th in the Eastern Conference at 10-14, with 23 points and 14 games separating it from the summit. The road win was sturdy, not transformative. Still, belief is a useful accelerant, and Rielly's timing could not be better. Now comes Pittsburgh tonight at 7 p.m. - a quick test of whether the Bruins win was a spark or merely a flash. Watch the blue line, and watch whether Toronto can make this two-game streak mean something.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The Blue Jays' winter has finally produced a jolt - and it comes from across the American League East. Toronto has agreed with Jazz Chisholm Jr. on a one-year deal guaranteeing $34.5 million, with a $16 million player option for 2028. That is not a cosmetic signing for a club whose season ended at -2.0 points; it is a bet on electricity, athleticism and an infielder capable of changing the temperature of a lineup. Chisholm brings star credentials, but also the volatility that makes this contract clever: Toronto gets immediate impact without surrendering long-term control. The player option can become a $40 million club option if he declines it, giving the Jays leverage while they rebuild an offence that plainly needs more life. Now comes the hard part - surround the new second baseman with dependable bats and pitching. Watch what Toronto does next before spring opens March 25 at Yankee Stadium.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The Raptors finally looked like a team tired of being pushed around - then the NBA Cup slammed the door anyway. Toronto thumped Brooklyn 124-100 on Friday, but was eliminated from Cup contention after Atlanta beat Boston. Scottie Barnes supplied the thunder with 34 points, while Immanuel Quickley delivered the sort of all-purpose command this club needs: 24 points, 10 rebounds and 14 assists. That makes the victory more than a pleasant November detour for a 7-11 team sitting fourth in the Atlantic, eight games behind; it is a glimpse of the ceiling buried inside an uneven start. The bruise beneath the celebration is Ja'Kobe Walter's right quad contusion, suffered in the third quarter and now another test for Toronto's depth. The Raptors have won two of their last three and own a one-game streak. Denver arrives Sunday at 6 p.m. ET - the Nuggets will reveal whether this was a turning point or merely a loud night against Brooklyn.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The Commanders have finally found a pulse, and now they must prove it travels. Washington's 22-20 victory over Cincinnati last Monday delivered a second straight win - a narrow escape, but a meaningful one for a club that has climbed to 4-5-1 and second place in the NFC East, two games behind the lead. The momentum is real; so is the margin for error. Brandon Aiyuk, newly added to the practice squad, will not make his Washington debut Sunday, delaying a potentially important boost for Jayden Daniels and the passing game. The defense faces its own test: cornerback Amik Robertson, still nursing an ankle injury, is out for a second consecutive game, forcing another reshuffle in the secondary. At Arizona on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET, the Commanders can make this winning streak a trend - or reveal it as a brief reprieve.

article.title: Maple Leafs Beat Bruins Behind Rielly
paragraphs: Morgan Rielly scored twice and the Maple Leafs beat the Bruins 3-1, with Colton Sissons adding a goal and an assist and Anthony Stolarz making 28 saves. Toronto visits the Penguins tonight at 7:00 p.m. ET on Sportsnet, with Tanev, Joshua and Roslovic out. The Leafs enter at 10-14, 12th in the Eastern Conference.

The Blue Jays are looking forward after agreeing to a one-year deal with Jazz Chisholm Jr. Their regular-season opener is at the Yankees on Thursday, March 25, at 1:35 p.m. ET. The Raptors beat the Nets 124-100 behind Scottie Barnes' 34 points and Immanuel Quickley's 10 rebounds and 14 assists. Toronto hosts Denver Sunday at 6:00 p.m. ET.
The Commanders visit the Cardinals Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox. Washington is 4-5-1 and second in the NFC East, while Brandon Aiyuk will not play.
